sentences.text: A Fabric data agent is like an analyst who turns your question into a query.
It only reads the data, never changes it, and uses your own permissions.
Imagine you ask a business question in plain language, and the agent takes care of querying the tables for you.
It can use up to five data sources, such as a warehouse, a lakehouse, Power B I semantic models, or K Q L databases.
It translates to S Q L, D A X, or K Q L, and always read-only.
Notice that every query is for reading, never for writing, and runs with the permissions of the person asking.
Answers are limited to twenty-five rows by twenty-five columns.
It works only in English, and you cannot change the language model.
If your question needs a huge table, remember this limit before you design the answer.
Think of short summaries, not endless lists.
It requires a paid Fabric capacity, F two or higher, or Power B I Premium with Fabric enabled.
In Copilot Studio, you add it as an external agent, in preview.
Check this with your organization's administrator before you start testing.
It cannot be the target of a Redirect node, it cannot be referenced in the instructions, and it does not work if the main agent is deployed in Microsoft Copilot.
Also, Agent evaluation does not support it.
Memorize these three limitations for the exam; they are asked often.
